subject: /tmp/opensip-implementation/m1-ts-runtime-subject-01
verdictScope: Trial exact-JSON codec and shape interpreter algorithms only. Not a generator, public API, Rust carrier, build/tool selection, or M1/release qualification.

requiredFindings.title: Regex dialect is unpinned and TS is more permissive than the reference on pinned path patterns
requiredFindings.detail: Pinned patterns use '.' and '$'. With the u flag, JS '.' does not match \r, U+2028 or U+2029, and JS '$' matches only at the end. Python re '.' excludes only \n, and '$' also matches before a final \n. On pinned schemas, TS accepts inputs that the Python reference rejects. That includes a parent-traversal path in the negative-lookahead CanonicalPath pattern. The 11191 generic cases, 43 metadata cases and my 1.47M harvested rows never contain line terminators, so none of them exposes this.

evidence.patternEdgeDifferential: 68640 rows (66 pinned patterns x edge strings), 428 mismatches in 4 patterns: '(^|/)\.\.?(/|$)' 2, CanonicalPath '...[^\u0000\\]*' 32, '...[^\u0000\\]+' 32, '^.+$' 362 (sarif-adapter:2 messageStrings patternProperties)
evidence.patternUsage: The CanonicalPath-style lookahead pattern appears at 34 pinned locations, and LogicalPath/not '(^|/)\.\.?(/|$)' at 4

requiredFindings.requiredChange: Pin one normative pattern dialect for the shared runtime and record who owns that decision (ECMA-262 as in 2020-12, or the reference behaviour). Then make TS, the Python reference and Rust agree, either by rewriting affected patterns to be terminator-explicit (for example [\s\S] instead of '.', (?![\s\S]) instead of '$') or by translating in the runtime. Add a retained line-terminator edge corpus (\n, \r, U+2028, U+2029, U+0085) over every pinned pattern to the differential.

requiredFindings.title: matches() checks an inertness profile but evaluates the live caller value; array prototype is not checked
requiredFindings.location: schema.ts:91 (canonical(value) result discarded), exact-json.ts:115-124 (no Array.prototype check)
requiredFindings.detail: canonical() rejects accessors and hidden or extra properties. It does not check array prototypes, and it cannot see Proxy traps. evaluate() then reads the original object with ordinary [[Get]] and calls item.every/item.some. So a value can pass the inert-data check and then show different data, or different methods, to the interpreter. Proxy traps also run during canonical(), which contradicts the no-effects ownership claim tested only for accessors.

evidence.arrayCustomPrototype: [1n,2n] with a prototype overriding every() matched {type:array, items:{type:string}} as true
evidence.arraySubclass: class X extends Array{every(){return true}} matched true
evidence.proxyInvalidToValid: Proxy over {a:5n} whose get trap returns 'x' matched {properties:{a:{type:string}},required:[a],additionalProperties:false} as true
evidence.proxyEffectsDuringCanonical: ownKeys trap invoked 3 times by canonical()

requiredFindings.requiredChange: Evaluate an owned snapshot (for example const owned = parseExact(canonical(value))), as the SchemaRegistry constructor already does, or accept only bytes. Require Object.getPrototypeOf(array) === Array.prototype in canonical(). Either reject Proxies where the host allows it (for example node:util types.isProxy) or explicitly scope the effect-free claim to non-Proxy inputs. Add regression tests for all three probes.

advisories.title: x-opensip-order data faults throw SchemaError and accept types the reference rejects
advisories.detail: ordered() throws SchemaError('invalid order key' or 'missing order key') for instance-dependent conditions such as utf8 over objects, mixed types, missing 'by' fields, or 'by' values that are arrays of unequal length. The reference treats these as invalid. Under not/anyOf/if the throw aborts evaluation instead of contributing false, which blurs the invalid-shape vs invalid-schema separation. It also accepts integers under utf8/path/ruleId/waiverId/predicate/{by}, and strings under numeric/candidateOrdinal, where the reference returns invalid. This is not reachable on current pins: 2680 targeted cases over all 134 non-sequence order nodes gave 0 mismatches, because items constraints in the same node run first. But allOf is evaluated before items (schema.ts:118 vs 133), so a sibling-branch layout would expose it. Recommend returning false with per-annotation type checks that match the reference.

advisories.title: Keyword value types are not validated in checkEntryPoints
advisories.detail: Malformed schema values fail open or coerce. Non-array enum and non-array required are ignored (both matched true). A bigint pattern is coerced to a RegExp. A string minimum uses JS mixed comparison. A non-string $ref throws TypeError instead of SchemaError. type 'number' is accepted by the keyword gate but never matches bigint. A static scan of the 28 pins found 0 malformed keyword values, no 'number' type, no nested $id, and no percent-encoded, array-index or non-exact refs, so this is latent. Add structural validation before this becomes shared runtime.

advisories.title: Non-productive reference cycles are reported as ShapeLimit
advisories.detail: {$id:'urn:cyc2', allOf:[{$ref:'urn:cyc2'}]} throws ShapeLimit, the same as the frozen self-ref check. A cycle that consumes no instance is a schema defect and can be detected statically in checkEntryPoints. The pinned closure contains only instance-consuming recursion (policy-document and policy-document:2 Predicate). 31-deep not-chains and 2^15-leaf and-trees finish without ShapeLimit.

advisories.title: 43-case metadata differential is not reproducible from frozen scripts
advisories.detail: schema-probe.mjs reads metadata-v1 sources.json and fixtures, writes schema-outcomes.json, and compares nothing. No frozen script produces schema-differential-02.json. I reproduced it on my own: with metadata-v2 pins, all 43 TS results equal both the v2 Resource-adapter Python results and the frozen expected list, and the v1 adapter differs on unsorted-help and duplicate-help-name. Freeze the script that actually produced the retained result.

advisories.title: Unmetered work and default limit are policy inputs
advisories.detail: The default limit of 1,000,000 raises ShapeLimit on a parsable ~2M-element integer array (about 781 ms). canonical(), regex, const/enum equality, required and the patternProperties inner loop are unmetered. They are bounded by input and schema size but are not logical work units. Regex wall-clock is, as stated, not bounded. Timings: 358784-key 4 MiB object parse 132 ms and canonical 497 ms; 2M-integer array parse 199 ms and canonical 707 ms.

advisories.title: Byte-input edge cases
advisories.detail: parseExact accepts a Uint8Array backed by SharedArrayBuffer, which another thread could mutate concurrently in worker contexts. The instanceof check rejects Uint8Array from another realm. Both are minor, but document the accepted input class.
